title: Parallel Token Prediction for Language Models
claim: A sequential decoder needs one step per token; our parallel model emits the same output in far fewer steps.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, large arrow labeled '35 → 5 steps' between them
description: Two rounded boxes side by side with a big green block arrow between them reading '35 → 5 steps'. The left box, outlined in orange and titled 'Autoregressive Model', shows a Python factorial function split into many small token chips. Only the first few tokens (the 'def factorial(num):' header) are shaded green. The rest of the function is gray, showing the steps still needed. The right box, outlined in green and titled 'Parallel Token Prediction (ours)', shows the same function as five wide green line-sized chips, so the whole function is already generated. The eye goes first to the arrow, then to the contrast between the mostly gray left panel and the fully green right panel.
caption: Our parallel model generates the same text as its teacher in a fraction of the steps. By the time our model (right) has generated an entire function, its autoregressive teacher (left) is still busy with the function header. Green tokens are generated during the time spent on PTP; gray tokens show the remaining steps an autoregressive model would still need. Prompt: Write a Python function that computes the factorial of a number.
abstract: Autoregressive decoding in language models is inherently slow, generating only one token per forward pass. We propose Parallel Token Prediction (PTP), a general-purpose framework for predicting multiple tokens in a single model call. PTP moves the source of randomness from post-hoc sampling to random input variables, making future tokens deterministic functions of those inputs and thus jointly predictable in a single forward pass. We prove that a single PTP call can represent arbitrary dependencies between tokens. PTP is trained by distilling an existing model or through inverse autoregressive training without a teacher. Experimentally, PTP achieves a 2.4x speedup on a diverse-task speculative decoding benchmark. We provide code and checkpoints at https://github.com/mandt-lab/ptp.
